findings.excerpt: noncomputable def freeHomEquiv : (freeObj F ⟶ G) ≃ (F ⟶ G.presheaf ⋙ forget _) where
findings.problem: `freeHomEquiv` has no simp interface. It is not `@[simps]` and has no hand-written `freeHomEquiv_symm_apply`. The sibling `ModuleCat.freeHomEquiv` is `@[simps]`. Its underlying data has simp lemmas: `freeObjDesc` is `@[simps]` and `freeAdjunctionUnit` is `@[simps]`. Despite that, users have to unfold the definition with `simp [freeHomEquiv, ...]` instead of using lemmas. This happens in this file, in `freeAdjunction` (`free_hom_ext (by ext; simp [freeHomEquiv, toPresheaf])`), and in Generator.lean's `freeYonedaEquiv_symm_app` (`simp [freeYonedaEquiv, freeHomEquiv, yonedaEquiv]`). Unfolding the definition exposes the `Equiv` structure and the `whiskerRight`/`toPresheaf` encoding. So `(freeHomEquiv.symm φ)` does not reduce to `freeObjDesc φ` in the normal form `simp` produces. The proofs on lines 89–90 also do not go through reusable lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simps]` to `freeHomEquiv`, or state the lemmas by hand. Put `freeHomEquiv_symm_apply : freeHomEquiv.symm φ = freeObjDesc φ` (or the `@[simps]`-generated version) in the simp set. Also add a lemma for `(freeHomEquiv ψ).app X` that is stated pointwise, e.g. `x ↦ ψ.app X (ModuleCat.freeMk x)`. Then drop `freeHomEquiv` from the `simp [freeHomEquiv, ...]` calls in `freeAdjunction` and in Generator.lean's `freeYonedaEquiv_symm_app`.
findings.benefit: Callers get a canonical normal form (`freeObjDesc φ`, or evaluation on `freeMk`) without unfolding the `Equiv` definition. This matches the already-`@[simps]` `ModuleCat.freeHomEquiv`. It also makes proofs such as `freeYonedaEquiv_symm_app` less dependent on the definition's internals.
